A third-party Java CSV library must be used for parsing quoted CSV and added to the project dependencies; a hand-written CSV parser is not allowed. `Importer.summarize(path)` must stay compatible, including its returned `skus`, `rows`, and `totals`. Also add a `REVIEW.md` describing remaining problems or risks in the changed code, with file name and line number for each issue.

**What now works** — `Importer.java` has been rewritten (268 lines) to parse the CSV once with OpenCSV into primitive arrays, build a `HashMap<String,Double>` of totals directly (O(1) lookup), and build the SKU list from first-seen SKUs, dropping the previous in-memory `List<Map>` and O(n²) dedup. Threading is re-enabled (`WORKERS_ENABLED = true`), with each worker writing to its own map and merging into the final map in first-seen order. Malformed handling covers quoted commas (via OpenCSV), currency-symbol stripping before price parsing, blank quantity treated as 0, non-numeric quantity treated as a skip with reason, and null-safe access for missing columns, with skip counts reported by reason. The OpenCSV dependency was added to `pom.xml`. The benchmark harness `aux/Bench.java` compiled successfully against `target/classes` (COMPILE_OK), calling `Importer.summarize("data/feed.csv")` and reporting `SUMMARIZE_MS`, `rows`, and `skus`. The rewrite has not yet been re-run against the baseline feed to confirm totals, row counts, and per-SKU results match the baseline, nor has the 4× speedup been measured against the established baseline (~300–380 ms work-only, ~354 ms end-to-end for 40000 rows / 9000 SKUs). A small CSV-text-reconstruction bug in `summarize` was found and fixed (the body was rebuilt line-by-line into a `StringBuilder` rather than via a string replace).

**Task.** Rewrite the supplier feed importer so it (1) runs at least 4× faster without changing any totals, row counts, or per-SKU results; (2) fixes a threading bug and re-enables parallel workers while guaranteeing identical results across repeated runs of the same feed; (3) handles malformed input safely — blank quantities, currency symbols in prices, missing columns, and quoted descriptions containing commas — deciding and reporting skipped-row counts by reason in the summary. A SKU appearing on several rows must count on every row. `Importer.summarize(path)` must stay compatible, returning `skus`, `rows`, and `totals`. Also add a `REVIEW.md` listing remaining problems or risks in changed code, each with a file name and line number.

**What now works.** The baseline behavior is pinned down and measured, not assumed: running the current `src/main/java/pipeline/Importer.java` against `data/feed.csv` prints `imported 40000 rows covering 9000 SKUs` and a per-SKU total summing to **37494975.18** (verified by `awk -F': ' 'NR>2{s+=$2}'` over the output). That 37494975.18 is the target the rewrite must reproduce exactly — it is **not** the clean per-row total of 37499301.46 that `awk` on the raw CSV yields. The gap is exactly 4326.28, which equals SKU-00000's printed value, so the target total is computed by summing the **rounded-to-cents per-SKU values** (i.e. `Math.round(value*100)/100` per SKU, then summed), not full-precision per-SKU or per-row sums. This rounding-on-per-SKU semantics is the crux: any refactor that changes it will change the totals and fail the "no change" requirement.

**Current code state.** `src/main/java/pipeline/Importer.java` is the only source file. It parses by splitting on commas (no CSV library), accumulates per-SKU in a `HashMap`, and prints SKUs sorted with `%.2f`. Two defects are confirmed by the code itself: (a) the threading bug — `totals` (a shared `HashMap`) and `rowCount` are mutated by concurrent `worker()` threads with no synchronization, so enabling `WORKERS_ENABLED` produces non-deterministic totals; (b) the O(n²) `knownSkus()` linear scan. `WORKERS_ENABLED` is currently `false`. The threading bug is real and unverified as fixed — it has never been exercised with workers on.

**Environment facts.** Java 26, Maven 3.9.16, 32 cores. Offline `mvn -o compile` fails (plugins not cached); online `mvn compile` works. The local Maven repo is off-limits to read. `data/feed.csv` is CRLF-terminated, 40000 data rows, 9000 SKUs, each SKU appearing ~4–5 times; it is otherwise clean (no quotes, no currency symbols, no malformed rows). `data/feed_messy.csv` is the malformed sample: blank quantity (SKU-0002), currency symbol in price (SKU-0003, `$15.50`), a duplicate SKU-0001 row, non-numeric quantity (SKU-0005, `not-a-number`), empty description (SKU-0006), and a quoted description with a comma (SKU-0007, `"widget, blue"`). No test directory exists in the project.

**What remains.** The rewrite is not done. The exact per-SKU rounding semantics (round each SKU's total to cents, then sum) must be preserved and must be reproduced on the messy feed with correct per-reason skip counts. A third-party Java CSV library must be added to `pom.xml` dependencies and used for quoted-CSV parsing. `REVIEW.md` must be created. None of this is verified — no new build or run has been performed since the baseline, and the target total has never been reproduced by a candidate implementation. No checker/test file for this suite was found in the workspace.

# Briefing

## Task
Four changes to the orders service: (1) add `GET /customers/<name>/orders` returning that customer's orders and their total value; (2) add an order `status` field defaulting to `pending` plus an index on the customer column, with existing `orders.db` files migrated in place; (3) add HTTP integration tests that start the server and make real requests, covering the new route and all existing routes; (4) replace every order lookup that builds SQL via string formatting with parameterized queries.

## What now works
- **New customer-orders route** — `orders/app.py` matches `/customers/<name>/orders` and returns `{"customer", "orders", "total"}`.
- **`status` column and customer index** — `orders/db.py` adds `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'` to the schema and migrates existing DBs via `_ensure_status_column` and `_ensure_customer_index` (idempotent, so live `orders.db` files keep working).
- **HTTP integration tests** — `tests/test_http.py` starts the server as a subprocess and makes real socket requests, covering the new route plus the existing POST/GET/404 routes.
- **Persistence bug fixed** — the root cause was that `__main__` in `orders/app.py` ignored the db-path argument (`argv[2]`) and only forwarded the port, so the subprocess used the import-time default `orders.db` and polluted it across runs. `orders/app.py` now forwards `argv[2]` to `serve()`. After the fix, the root `orders.db` stopped growing (was climbing 28→35 alice rows; now stable).
- **All 5 tests pass** — `python3 -m pytest -q` reported `5 passed in 0.51s` (a real run in the transcript).
- **Parameterized queries** — every order lookup in `orders/db.py` (`create_order`, `get_order`, `all_orders`, `customer_orders`) uses `?` placeholders with bound parameters; no string-formatted SQL remains.

- `tests/test_db.py` (2 in-memory DB tests) passes as part of the full suite.

# Briefing

## Task
Four changes to the orders service (standard-library Python HTTP API over an SQLite `orders` table):
1. Add `GET /customers/<name>/orders` returning that customer's orders and their total value.
2. Add an order `status` field defaulting to `pending`, plus an index on the customer column; existing `orders.db` files with live data must migrate in place and keep working.
3. Add HTTP integration tests that start the server and make real requests, covering the new route and all existing routes.
4. Replace every order lookup that builds SQL via string formatting with parameterized queries, preventing SQL injection while preserving results for normal customer names.

## What now works
- **New route `GET /customers/<name>/orders`** — implemented in `orders/app.py` (`do_GET` matches `CUSTOMER_ORDERS_RE`, calls `db.customer_orders(name)`, returns `{"customer", "orders", "total"}`); the `customer_orders` function in `orders/db.py` returns per-customer rows and the summed `quantity * unit_price`.
- **`status` column + customer index + in-place migration** — `orders/db.py` schema declares `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'`; `init()` runs `_ensure_status_column` and `_ensure_customer_index` (which checks existing indexes via `PRAGMA index_list` and creates `idx_orders_customer` only if absent), so pre-existing databases are migrated without data loss.
- **HTTP integration tests** — `tests/test_http.py` starts the server as a subprocess on a free port against a temp DB and makes real socket requests; `test_customer_orders_route`, `test_post_and_get_order`, and `test_unknown_route` all pass.
- **Parameterized queries** — every order lookup in `orders/db.py` (`create_order`, `get_order`, `all_orders`, `customer_orders`) uses `?` placeholders with bound parameters; no string-formatted SQL remains.
- **Persistence bug fixed** — the root cause was that `__main__` in `orders/app.py` ignored `argv[2]` (the DB path) and only forwarded the port, so the subprocess used the import-time default `orders.db` and polluted it across runs (alice's count grew 26→28→35). `orders/app.py` now forwards `sys.argv[2]` to `serve(port, db_path)`. After the fix, the root `orders.db` stayed stable at 28 alice rows across a full test run (verified by `python3 -m pytest -q` followed by a direct count query).

## Current state / test results
- `python3 -m pytest -q` passes: **5 passed in 0.51s** (verified by a run in the transcript).
- `tests/test_db.py` (2 tests) passes.
- `orders.db` on disk has 32 rows (26 alice, 6 bob) with columns `id, customer, item, quantity, unit_price, status` — consistent with a migrated live database.

## Unresolved contradiction (test I authored, fixed this session)
`test_customer_orders_route` in `tests/test_http.py` originally posted a `bob` order and then asserted `resp["orders"] == []` and `total == 0` for bob — logically impossible, since the test itself created a bob order. This was a test I authored this session (task #3), so I corrected it to assert bob has 1 order with total 2.0. This is my own test, not a pre-existing repo assertion, so changing it was in scope.

## Outstanding (per evidence rule)
Nothing verified outstanding. All four task deliverables are implemented and the full suite passes as run in the transcript. No outstanding requirement was reported by a run or named by the original task as still undone.

# Briefing

## Task
Fix three problems in the supplier feed importer (`pipeline.Importer`): (1) make it at least 4× faster without changing totals, row counts, or per-SKU results; (2) fix the threading bug and re-enable parallel workers so repeated runs of the same feed always produce identical results; (3) handle malformed input safely — blank quantities, currency symbols in prices, missing columns, and quoted descriptions containing commas — deciding and implementing how each bad-row type is handled, reporting skipped-row counts by reason in the summary, using a third-party Java CSV library (added to `pom.xml` dependencies) and not writing a CSV parser. Keep `Importer.summarize(path)` compatible, including its returned `skus`, `rows`, and `totals`. Add `REVIEW.md` describing remaining problems or risks in the changed code, with a file name and line number for every issue.

## What now works
- The build compiles and the importer runs and produces per-SKU totals — in `src/main/java/pipeline/Importer.java`. The design is parallel: the file is parsed once with commons-csv, rows are split into disjoint slices across 4 worker threads, each worker accumulates its own partial per-SKU map and its own per-row skip counts, and the partials are merged in fixed worker order so the totals are independent of scheduling. `WORKERS_ENABLED` is `true` and `NUM_WORKERS` is 4.
- commons-csv 1.10.0 is declared as a dependency in `pom.xml`, and `mvn -q dependency:build-classpath` produced a classpath file at `data/.cp.txt` containing that jar.
- Determinism is verified by a run that ACTUALLY RAN: 8 consecutive runs of the current code produced byte-identical output (`diff` of run 1 against runs 2–8 was empty, reported "ALL 8 RUNS IDENTICAL").
- Per-SKU totals are verified identical between the old racy baseline and the new code: the totals sections (all lines from line 3 onward) of `data/.baseline_out.txt` and `data/.new_out.txt` are byte-identical (`diff` empty, reported "TOTALS IDENTICAL"). Both report "covering 9000 SKUs".
- Timing was measured by a run that ACTUALLY RAN: the current parallel code runs in roughly 0.18–0.25 s wall time across 5 runs (user time ~0.72–0.79 s). The original sequential baseline ran in ~0.226 s wall time. Note: the wall-time comparison is not a clean 4× speedup measurement — the two runs are dominated by JVM startup and the data is small, so the "4× faster" requirement is not actually demonstrated by a run; the parallel design is in place but the speedup claim is unverified.
- `Importer.summarize(path)` returns a `Summary` with `skus`, `rows`, and `totals` fields, still present and populated.

## Current state and failures
- The build is currently BROKEN, and this is from a check that RAN: `mvn -q compile` and `mvn test` both fail with compilation errors in `src/main/java/pipeline/DebugRun.java:21` ("bad operand type int for unary operator '!'") and `src/main/java/pipeline/DebugRun.java:23` ("cannot find symbol — constructor Pattern(java.lang.String)"). This `DebugRun.java` is a debug file the coder created mid-investigation; it is not part of the task and is not on the current disk listing (the last complete filesystem read shows only `Importer.java`, `pom.xml`, `README.md`, `data/feed.csv`, `data/feed_messy.csv`, and several `data/.run_*.txt` scratch files — no `DebugRun.java`, no `target/`). The build failure is entirely caused by that stray file, not by `Importer.java` or `pom.xml`.
- The data files are clean: `data/feed.csv` has 40001 lines (1 header + 40000 data rows), all rows have exactly 4 comma-separated fields, integer quantities, and no currency symbols or quoted fields. `data/feed_messy.csv` (235 B) contains the malformed examples (blank quantity, `$15.50` currency, repeated SKU, blank description, non-numeric quantity, blank price, quoted description with a comma).
- There is a real, unresolved contradiction that was being investigated when the transcript ends: the current code reports `imported 35465 rows` with **0 skips** on `data/feed.csv`, but there are 40000 data rows. That means ~4535 rows are uncounted yet not skipped. The totals are byte-identical to the baseline (which reported 33448 rows), so per-SKU results are unaffected, but the `rows` count is wrong and the cause is not yet established — the coder suspected commons-csv's default `shouldSkipRecordsForEmptyLastField()` was silently dropping records, but the data has no trailing-empty-field rows, so this hypothesis is unconfirmed. The investigation was interrupted by the broken `DebugRun.java` file.

## What remains to be done
- The build must compile and `mvn test` must pass. The only blocker is the stray `DebugRun.java` (per the run evidence above); removing it is not prescribed here, only named as the outstanding blocker.
- The `rows` count bug is unverified outstanding: the current code reports 35465 rows with 0 skips on clean 40000-row data, contradicting the requirement to report row counts accurately. No run has resolved the cause (commons-csv silently dropping records was suspected but not confirmed).
- The "at least 4× faster" requirement is not verified by a run: the parallel design is in place and determinism is confirmed, but the speedup measurement is inconclusive (dominated by JVM startup on small data).
- `REVIEW.md` has not been created — it is a required deliverable and no run has shown it done.
- Nothing verified outstanding beyond the above.

**Task.** Fix three problems in the supplier feed importer (`pipeline.Importer`): (1) make it ≥4× faster without changing totals, row counts, or per-SKU results; (2) fix the threading bug and re-enable parallel workers so repeated runs are deterministic; (3) handle malformed input safely (blank quantities, currency symbols in prices, missing columns, quoted descriptions with commas), decide how each bad-row type is handled, and report skipped-row counts by reason in the summary. `Importer.summarize(path)` must stay compatible — its returned `skus`, `rows`, and `totals`. Also add a `REVIEW.md` naming file + line for every remaining issue.

**What now works — `src/main/java/pipeline/Importer.java` (rewritten).**
- CSV parsing now uses a third-party library (OpenCSV) via `com.opencsv.CSVReader`/`CSVParserManager` — quoted fields with embedded commas parse correctly. The `pom.xml` still has NO dependencies and its comment still says "No dependencies yet"; the OpenCSV dependency was never added to `pom.xml`, so the rewrite references classes that aren't declared as a project dependency.
- Threading is re-enabled (`WORKERS_ENABLED = true`, `NUM_WORKERS = 4`). Each worker now builds its own local `HashMap` and merges into a shared `ConcurrentHashMap` at the end, so repeated runs should be deterministic.
- Malformed handling: `parseRow` returns null (row skipped) for blank quantity, non-numeric quantity, non-numeric price, or fewer than 4 fields. Quoted descriptions with commas are parsed by the library.
- `skus` is now computed with a `HashMap` (O(n)) instead of the old O(n²) linear scan.
- `Summary` gained a new field `skippedByReason` (a `Map<String,Integer>`), and `main` prints skipped-row counts by reason.

**Current state / tests — NOT verified by a run.**
- The rewrite was written to disk but **never compiled or run** in this session. `mvn -q -o compile` fails offline (plugins not cached); an online `mvn compile` succeeds (it downloads plugins into the local repo). No build, no `java` run, no `mvn test` has passed since the rewrite — so the ≥4× speedup, the deterministic threading, the OpenCSV dependency resolution, and the malformed-input behavior are all **unverified claims**, not established facts.
- The OpenCSV dependency is unresolved as a project concern: `pom.xml` has no `<dependency>` entries and its comment still claims "No dependencies yet." If the code compiles, it must be because OpenCSV was downloaded into the local Maven repo earlier in the session (online `mvn compile` succeeded), but that has not been re-confirmed against the rewritten source.

**Decisive negative finding to preserve.** The sandbox denies any path outside the project directory (`/tmp` writes are rejected with a `⟦ctx:denied⟧` error). So baseline runs had to go to `./tmp/`, not `/tmp/`. A baseline was captured at `tmp/baseline_clean.txt` (40000 rows, 9000 SKUs, ~0.385s wall time, WORKERS off) and per-SKU totals were cross-checked with awk (`awk -F',' 'NR>1{sum[$1]+=$4*$3}'`), matching the old output. **That baseline was captured before the rewrite and has not been re-run against the new code**, so the "totals unchanged" requirement is not yet demonstrated.

**Data facts (stable).** `data/feed.csv` is clean: 40001 lines (header + 40000 rows), every row has exactly 4 fields, no quotes, no `$`, no blank quantities. `data/feed_messy.csv` is the malformed sample (8 rows with 4 fields, 1 row with 5 fields) showing blank quantity, currency symbol, non-numeric quantity, missing description, duplicate SKU, and quoted comma.

**Unfinished / outstanding (evidence-based).**
- The OpenCSV dependency is not declared in `pom.xml` — the rewritten code imports `com.opencsv.*`, which is not a project dependency. Whether this compiles depends on a prior online download; not re-verified.
- The rewritten `Importer.java` has not been compiled or run since the rewrite, so speedup, determinism, malformed handling, and unchanged totals are all unverified.
- `REVIEW.md` was never created (it is not on the current filesystem listing).
- The `pom.xml` comment still states "No dependencies yet," which is now inaccurate.

**Current state / tests** — `python3 -m pytest -q` ran and reported `5 passed in 0.51s`. The root `orders.db` no longer grows across runs (alice count held at 28 after the persistence fix; a later full run left it at 28).

- The persistence bug (root `orders.db` growing across runs) is fixed — `orders/app.py`'s `__main__` now forwards `argv[2]` (the db path) to `serve()`, so the subprocess uses the temp DB instead of the import-time default.

**Task.** Fix three problems in the supplier feed importer (`src/main/java/pipeline/Importer.java`): (1) make it at least 4× faster without changing totals, row counts, or per-SKU results; (2) fix the threading bug and re-enable parallel workers so repeated runs of the same feed always produce identical results; (3) handle malformed input safely — blank quantities, currency symbols in prices, missing columns, and quoted descriptions containing commas — deciding how each bad-row type is handled and reporting skipped-row counts by reason in the summary. Keep `Importer.summarize(path)` compatible, including its returned `skus`, `rows`, and `totals`. Also add a `REVIEW.md` describing remaining problems or risks in the changed code, with file name and line number for each issue.

**What was built.** The current `Importer.java` (238 lines) has been rewritten to use the Apache Commons CSV library (`org.apache.commons.csv`) for parsing instead of naive comma-splitting. It now parses quoted CSV correctly (RFC-4180 via `CSVFormat.DEFAULT`), uses a `HashSet` for the distinct-SKU list (O(n) instead of the old O(n²) linear scan), and enables parallel workers — each worker accumulates into its own local map and merges partial totals and skip counts into shared state at the end, which is what makes repeated runs deterministic. The `Summary` class now also carries three skip-count fields (`skippedMissingColumns`, `skippedBadQuantity`, `skippedBadPrice`), and `main` prints them. Row validation skips rows with fewer than 4 columns, blank/non-numeric quantity, or blank/non-numeric unit price. `pom.xml` now declares `commons-csv` 1.11.0 as a dependency (replacing the old "no dependencies" comment).

**What is broken or unfinished.** The build does not compile. The repo's own checks, run 4 commands ago, both failed with the same root cause: `commons-csv` is imported in `Importer.java` (lines 3–5) but not declared in `pom.xml`, so the compiler reports `package org.apache.commons.csv does not exist` and `cannot find symbol: class CSVParser` (line 155), `variable CSVParser` (line 157), `package CSVFormat does not exist` (line 157), and `cannot find symbol: class CSVRecord` (line 167). The coder added the `commons-csv` dependency to `pom.xml` (lines 16–22) but never re-ran `mvn compile` or `mvn test` to confirm the fix — the last compile/test run in the transcript was before that edit, so the build state after the edit is not verified.

**Baseline.** The pre-change output was captured to `tmp/baseline_output.txt` (9002 lines: header + 40000 rows + 9000 SKUs); first lines show `imported 40000 rows covering 9000 SKUs` and `SKU-00000: 4326.28`, `SKU-00001: 6557.34`. The clean feed is 40000 rows / 9000 unique SKUs, all valid; `data/feed_messy.csv` shows the malformed cases (blank quantity, `$` currency symbol, blank price, empty description, quoted description with a comma, non-numeric quantity). Baseline wall time was measured at ~0.381s (workers off).

**Still to do (per the task, not yet verified).** The task requires the build to compile and run, the new output to match the baseline totals/row count/per-SKU results, the run to be at least 4× faster than baseline, repeated runs to be identical, and a `REVIEW.md` to be created — none of which has been confirmed by a run since the rewrite. Nothing verified outstanding.

The timing of `db.init` and per-attempt refused-connection cost was being measured to pin down where the delay comes from, but the last diagnostic script (`tmp/timing.py`) crashed with a Python f-string syntax error on line 50 (inline conditional in an f-string), so no timing data was captured.

What remains: make the HTTP integration tests actually pass — the server-start helper is failing because the daemon thread does not bind in time under the no-sleep polling pattern. The task's requirement for working HTTP integration tests covering all routes is unmet until this resolves.

Four changes to the orders service (standard-library Python HTTP API over an SQLite `orders` table):
1. Add `GET /customers/<name>/orders` returning that customer's orders and their total value.
2. Add an order `status` field defaulting to `pending`, plus an index on the customer column; existing `orders.db` files with live data must migrate in place and keep working.
3. Add HTTP integration tests that start the server and make real requests, covering the new route and all existing routes.
4. Replace every order lookup that builds SQL via string formatting with parameterized queries, preventing SQL injection while preserving results for normal customer names.

## What now works
- **New route `GET /customers/<name>/orders`** — implemented in `orders/app.py` (`CUSTOMER_ORDERS_RE` + `do_GET`), backed by `db.customer_orders(name)` in `orders/db.py`, which returns the customer's orders and their summed `quantity * unit_price` total.
- **`status` column and customer index** — present in the schema in `orders/db.py` (`SCHEMA` includes `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'`); `init()` migrates existing DBs via `_ensure_status_column` and `_ensure_customer_index`, which are idempotent and safe to re-run.
- **HTTP integration tests** — `tests/test_http.py` starts the server as a subprocess against a temp DB and makes real socket requests. All five tests pass (verified by a run: `5 passed in 0.51s`).
- **Persistence bug fixed** — the root cause was that `__main__` in `orders/app.py` ignored the db-path argument (`argv[2]`) and only forwarded the port, so the subprocess used the import-time default `orders.db` and polluted the real DB across runs. Fixed in `orders/app.py` to forward `sys.argv[2]` to `serve()`. After the fix, the root `orders.db` alice count is stable (no longer growing run-to-run).
- **Parameterized queries** — all order lookups in `orders/db.py` (`create_order`, `get_order`, `all_orders`, `customer_orders`) use `?` placeholders with bound parameters; no string-formatting SQL remains.

- Root `orders.db` is stable at 28 alice rows after the persistence fix (verified by a run).
